thread: Style Guide for Python Code: In Python, this style is generally deemed unnecessary because attribute and method names are prefixed with an object, and function names are prefixed with a module name. 🧵
2/ The Python standard library is conservative and requires limiting lines to 79 characters.
3/ In Python code, it is permissible to break before or after a binary operator, as long as the convention is consistent locally.
4/ Module level "dunders" such as __all__, __author__, __version__, etc. should be placed after the module docstring but before any import statements except from __future__ imports.
5/ Each line of a block comment starts with a # and a single space.
6/ Full post, worth reading in full: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/python/peps/main/peps/pep-0008.rst
linkedin:
In Python, this style is generally deemed unnecessary because attribute and method names are prefixed with an object, and function names are prefixed with a module name.

I just read "Style Guide for Python Code" and the core idea is worth sharing. Three takeaways:

✅ The Python standard library is conservative and requires limiting lines to 79 characters.
✅ In Python code, it is permissible to break before or after a binary operator, as long as the convention is consistent locally.
✅ Module level "dunders" such as __all__, __author__, __version__, etc. should be placed after the module docstring but before any import statements except from __future__ imports.

Which of these matches your experience with names?
